Department Information
Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Do you set high standards for yourself and enjoy a collaborative and challenging work environment? The mission of the California Department of Social Services is to serve, protect, and support the people of California experiencing need in ways that empower wellbeing and disrupt systemic inequities. The vision of the California Department of Social Services is to provide quality services with a commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and equitable California where all people can thrive.

The Research, Automation, and Data Division’s (RADDs) mission is to improve the way the Department collects, manages, and deploys data to support the efficient, effective, and equitable delivery of government social services. RADD manages major statewide initiatives to streamline and automate eligibility determination and benefit administration for key safety net programs, and leads efforts such as human-centered design, data governance, automation and continuous quality improvement, data visualization and analysis, and research partnerships to improve client outcomes and promote program integrity. Across these efforts, RADD provides coaching to the Department on all aspects of the data lifecycle.

CDSS Guiding Principles

Diversity. Equity. Inclusion. Accessibility. Belonging.
We ensure opportunities for everyone to participate in a meaningful way in fulfilling the mission and vision of CDSS.

Community Engagement
We prioritize the lived experiences of community members as a driving force behind the creation, implementation, desired impact, or change of programs and services.

Empowerment
We engage, operate, and advocate from the understanding that each community and person have desires and capabilities to lead in their own life.

Quality Services
We provide services that align intent and impact by ensuring that they are accessible, community driven, interconnected, and continuously improved.

Data Defined Outcomes
We equitably collect and analyze data, take data-driven action, and measure outcomes relevant to those we serve, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Job Description And Duties
Are you ready to champion data that drives real change for California families? Join the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Specialist II, where you’ll transform raw data into accurate, timely data products that influence policy decisions, support budget development, and inform how counties deliver critical services. As part of the Research, Automation & Data Division (RADD), and the Research & Data Insights (RDI) Branch, you will contribute to CDSS’s mission of building a sustainable, data-driven culture. You’ll play a pivotal role in producing accurate data required for State and Federal reporting, supporting program partners, and improving outcomes for vulnerable families statewide.

What You’ll Do

Serve as a technical lead for advanced data engineering, data management, and statistical analysis across major social service programs including child welfare, Temporary Aid for Needy Families (TANF), and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
Build and maintain complex reporting pipelines in Snowflake, extracting, validating, and reconciling data from multiple systems to meet detailed State and Federal reporting requirements. Produce compliant, audit-ready reporting files with robust documentation of methodologies and transformations.
Develop original statistical programming and analytical code using SQL (Snowflake), Python, and R. Design reusable datasets, views, and stored procedures; perform sophisticated joins, window functions, and semi-structured data processing. Produce high-quality insights for program oversight, evaluation, and policy development.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to Research Data Analysts II and Research Data Specialists I, supporting skill development in coding, analytics, and reporting standards. Lead limited-term projects with teams of up to six researchers.

Why Join Us?

Play a key role in building CDSS’s modern, statewide data ecosystem.
Influence high-visibility reporting and analytical work that shapes policy and funding decisions affecting millions.
Collaborate in a mission-driven environment that values innovation, transparency, and human-centered design.
Grow your technical and leadership impact while helping California deliver better services to its most vulnerable populations.

The Department of Social Services does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment.

What We Do

As a premier provider of environmental services in the Western United States, Patriot Environmental Services
provides a wide range of industrial, emergency response and remediation services. We are committed to the principles of safety, superior customer service and experience, and unyielding quality and dedication. We provide a broad array of environmental services to meet any need that our clients may have. From emergency spill response to hazardous waste transportation to wastewater treatment, or from industrial cleaning to full facility closure and remediation, Patriot can do it all with our own internal resources and do so while accomplishing every metric of success.

Our mission is to always be Prepared and Professional.

Join the team that makes a difference!

Duties And Responsibilities

Ensure that Health and Safety is the number one priority by complying with all safe work practices, policies, processes, and acting in a safe manner.
Perform emergency response cleanup activities including but not limited to chemical and water spills, non-hazardous and hazardous waste and toxic materials and equipment decontamination.
Sweep, dig, shovel, lift, pressure wash and handling drums to assist in cleanup.
Operate cleanup equipment used in hazardous waste activities.
Follow policies and procedures for control and storage of hazardous substances.
Attend safety training as required.
Comply with the Random Drug Testing Program.

Experience, Education And Requirements

High school diploma or GED preferred.
Some environmental services industry experience preferred.
Some hazardous waste control experience preferred.
Valid driver’s license required.
Driving record that meets company standards and current DMV printout, required.
40-hour HAZWOPER certification required.
Confined Space Entry certification preferred.

Skills And Competencies

Strong attention to detail; meticulous.
Safety conscious.
Patient
Flexible to fast paced changes.

Required to wear a variety of personal protection equipment as required including but not limited to Tyvek suits.
Required to wear respirators as needed.
Performs labor intensive activities in all weather conditions during any hours during the day or night.

Benefits

PTO, paid holidays, sick time
Medical, dental, vision, life insurances
401(k) with company matching

jobs.description:
This is a job that Jill, our AI Recruiter, is recruiting for on behalf of one of our customers.

She will pick the best candidates from Jack's network.

The next step is to speak to Jack.

Job Title

Customer Success Engineer

Salary

$130k-$180k + Equity

Company Description

Tasklet is a $20M venture-backed AI startup in San Francisco, funded by Union Square Ventures, Lightspeed, and Y Combinator. Founded by the creators of Firebase and Shortwave, Tasklet is building an autonomous agent platform that allows companies to run complex business operations using plain English outcomes.

Job Description

As a Customer Success Engineer at Tasklet, you will bridge the gap between technical complexity and user success. You'll own the customer journey, from high-touch onboarding to solving intricate technical issues. By automating support workflows with AI and feeding insights back to engineering, you’ll ensure our users thrive while scaling our operations efficiently.

Location

San Francisco, USA

Why this role is remarkable

Join a high-growth AI startup backed by elite investors like Union Square Ventures and Lightspeed, currently valued at $175M.
Work directly with a world-class founding team that previously built Firebase (acquired by Google) and Shortwave.
Shape the future of AI agents by using Tasklet's own technology to automate your role and improve the product.

What You Will Do

Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues across external services, code execution, and web browsing tasks.
Manage high-touch customer relationships through onboarding, demos, and proactive training to ensure long-term product success.
Collaborate with engineering to fix product bugs and build internal tools like dashboards and AI-augmented support workflows.

The ideal candidate

Possesses 1-5 years of experience in high-agency, customer-facing roles within a fast-paced technology or startup environment.
Demonstrates a "power user" technical mindset with a passion for automating repetitive work using modern AI tools.
Excellent communicator who can translate complex technical concepts into clear, empathetic, and persuasive guidance for business users.

Who are Jack & Jill?

Ok, I'll go first. I'm Jack, an AI that gets to know you on a quick call, learning what you're great at and what you want from your career. Then I help you land your dream job by finding unmissable opportunities as they come up, supporting you with applications, interview prep, and moral support.

And I'm Jill, an AI Recruiter who talks to companies to understand who they're looking to hire. Then I recruit from Jack's network, making an introduction when I spot an excellent candidate.

How does this work?

Jack's an AI agent for job searching and career coaching. He works for you.
Jill is the AI recruiter working for the company. She recruits from Jack's network.
If it's a match and the company wants to meet you, they'll make the intro. In the meantime, if you'd like, Jack will send you excellent alternatives.

We never post fake jobs

This isn't a trick. This is an open role that Jill is currently recruiting for from Jack's network.

Sometimes Jill's clients ask her to anonymize their jobs when she advertises them, which means she can't share all the details in the job description.

We appreciate this can make them look a bit suspect, but there isn't much we can do about it.

Give Jack a spin! You could land this role. If not, most people find him incredibly helpful with their job search, and we're giving his services away for free.

Description

INTERA is seeking a Geologist / Hydrogeologist / Geophysicist for our Austin office to support groundwater, water supply, environmental, and subsurface characterization projects throughout Texas and the western United States. This is a primarily desktop-based role centered on data interpretation, modeling, analysis, and technical reporting rather than field work. The role suits an early- to mid-career professional with 2–5 years of applied experience in geology, hydrogeology, geophysics, petrophysics, geological or petroleum engineering, environmental consulting, or a related subsurface discipline who wants to broaden their technical expertise alongside experienced practitioners in these fields.

Key Responsibilities

Subsurface Characterization and Interpretation

Interpret borehole geophysical logs (gamma ray, spontaneous potential, resistivity, density, neutron, sonic, acoustic, and caliper) and petrophysical datasets to evaluate lithology, porosity, permeability, fracture occurrence, aquifer and production-zone properties, water-quality indicators, and subsurface heterogeneity.
Develop and calibrate petrophysical models from borehole geophysical log data for geologic property characterization, groundwater quality estimations, and environmental investigations.
Interpret geologic, hydrostratigraphic, and structural relationships from borehole logs, geologic maps, and geophysical data; characterize alluvial, sedimentary, carbonate, fractured-rock, and mixed aquifer systems; and identify hydrostratigraphic units, aquifer boundaries, and groundwater-quality trends.
Develop cross sections, hydrostratigraphic frameworks, fence diagrams, and conceptual site and digital subsurface models, integrating borehole logs, core and laboratory analyses, drilling data, geophysical surveys, and aquifer testing and monitoring results into defensible interpretations and recommendations.
Support well siting, well design, and aquifer characterization through geologic, geophysical, and petrophysical analysis.

Groundwater Studies and Numerical Modeling

Support groundwater resource evaluations, water supply development studies, and aquifer characterization projects.
Compile and interpret groundwater level, pumping, aquifer test, recharge, and water-quality datasets to assess aquifer properties, groundwater availability, well performance, and sustainability.
Support development of hydrogeologic conceptual models used for water resource planning, groundwater management, and environmental investigations.
Support the groundwater modeling team with the development, calibration, and interpretation of groundwater flow, contaminant transport, subsidence, and subsurface process models using finite difference, finite element, or related numerical techniques.
Assist with sensitivity analyses, history matching, uncertainty evaluations, and predictive simulations, and prepare summaries that communicate model assumptions, results, and limitations.

Data Analysis, GIS, and Workflows

Manage, analyze, and visualize subsurface and water-quality datasets, applying quantitative, statistical, and machine-learning methods to evaluate trends and support predictive modeling.
Develop maps, cross sections, dashboards, and figures to communicate project findings, using GIS software for spatial analysis and data management.
Develop automated, reproducible workflows for interpretation, visualization, and analysis using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.

Reporting and Communication

Prepare technical memoranda, reports, figures, and presentations, and clearly communicate findings to project teams, clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
Support proposals, work plans, cost estimates, and deliverables, and participate in technical reviews and quality assurance/quality control.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Geological Engineering, Geophysics, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.
2–5 years of professional or graduate-level experience in hydrogeology, geology, groundwater investigations, geophysical interpretation, environmental consulting, or subsurface characterization.
Experience evaluating and interpreting complex subsurface and water-quality datasets, including borehole geophysical logs and petrophysical interpretation, to characterize subsurface systems and support technical decision-making.
Understanding of hydrogeologic principles including groundwater flow, aquifer characterization, recharge, aquifer testing, and water supply development, and experience developing cross sections, hydrostratigraphic frameworks, and conceptual site models.
Working knowledge of subsurface-based geophysical investigation and interpretation methods, including borehole logging and 2D/3D seismic.
Experience using Python, MATLAB, or similar scientific computing tools, and ArcGIS Pro and/or QGIS, for data analysis, visualization, automation, modeling, and spatial analysis.
Strong quantitative, analytical, technical writing, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and within multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Geologist (PG) license, or ability to obtain licensure within a reasonable timeframe.
Master's degree or PhD in Geology, Hydrogeology, Geophysics, Geological Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
Experience supporting groundwater supply development, well siting, aquifer storage and recovery (ASR), groundwater management, or water resource planning projects.
Experience interpreting borehole geophysical logs, applying petrophysical methods, and integrating subsurface, groundwater chemistry, and water-quality datasets into conceptual site models.
Familiarity with groundwater flow modeling and MODFLOW-based models, numerical simulation, porous-media flow, or reservoir characterization.
Proficiency with Python, MATLAB, or similar languages, and with PETRA, Leapfrog, ArcGIS Pro, Techlog, Interactive Petrophysics (IP), Petrel, or similar interpretation and modeling software.
Experience interpreting laboratory, core analysis, and petrophysical measurement data, and supporting environmental remediation, energy, geothermal, mining, carbon management, subsurface storage, or water-resource development projects, including proposal preparation and client interaction.

INTERA Incorporated is seeking a senior-level Geologist and Drilling Coordinator to join its Mining and Environmental Line of Business in the Albuquerque, New Mexico office. The position also supports clients in meeting regulatory requirements, restoring impacted sites, and sustainably managing natural resources.

This position will include implementing highly technical work plans for complex projects, serving as the primary link between field operations and the project manager while leading teams of personnel to conduct field and office support work for subsurface contamination investigations, geotechnical studies, groundwater monitoring well installation and development, etc. Clients include state and municipal agencies and private industries that share our values of environmental stewardship and technical excellence.

Lead daily site activities, manage field crews, and oversee work performed by drilling contractors and subcontractors to ensure work is completed in accordance with workplans, design drawings, specifications, and client expectations.
Ensure compliance with health and safety requirements for fieldwork.
Collect environmental samples (soil/rock, aqueous, vapor), oversee drilling soil borings and monitoring well installation, and conduct hydraulic testing.
Ensure accuracy of drilling data and submit status reports to the Project Manager.
Develop cost estimates and proposals for drilling projects, including acquiring bids from multiple drilling firms and other vendors while ensuring consistency between and amongst the bids.
Plan drilling programs including resource and equipment needs, preparation of field implementation plans that reference standard operation procedures (SOPs), sampling and analysis plans, and Health and Safety plans.

Log soil and rock core utilizing ASTM standards for lithologic interpretation and prepare boring logs.
Analyze environmental data and author detailed technical reports.
Participate in environmental site characterization investigations, including soil gas investigations, soil sampling, and groundwater sampling.
Continue to build upon and refine INTERA’s approach to drilling operations, including updating SOP’s and identifying potential inefficiencies.
Mentor junior staff and collaborate with technical teams across the company.
Support business development by maintaining client relationships and identifying new opportunities. Maintain regular contact with an ever-increasing list of drillers and related contractors.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, or related field.
10+ years of relevant professional experience with increasing levels of responsibility.
Professional licensure or willingness to obtain.
Proficiency in various borehole advancement methods, including but not limited to sonic, hollow stem auger, direct push, air rotary casing hammer, and flooded reverse circulation mud rotary.
Demonstrated experience managing drilling projects.
Strong leadership, technical report writing, problem-solving, and verbal communication skills with the ability to convey complex thoughts and ideas in a clear and concise manner.
General knowledge of hydrogeology, nature, and extent of contamination evaluation.
The ability to work with a project team or independently to complete technical work.
Experience developing and maintaining long-lasting relationships with drilling firms.
Experience analyzing geophysical logs.
Willingness to travel to project sites (50% - 70%) and other INTERA offices (primarily within New Mexico and Texas).

Master’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, or related field.
Familiarity with state and federal environmental regulations (e.g., RCRA, CERCLA, NMED/NMAC, OSE, EPA) and risk-based criteria.
Proficiency in various environmental sampling techniques such as heated head space soil sampling, soil sampling, push-ahead groundwater sampling, and zonal groundwater sampling.
Experience with pLog and Logplot software.
Previous experience with aquifer test (Aqtesolv, nSIGHTS) and geologic modeling software (Leapfrog preferred)
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER Certification

Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Field Technician I to join our team and support engineering, environmental services, materials testing, and inspection projects. In this role, you will conduct on-site inspections, materials testing, and environmental sampling to ensure construction, infrastructure, and environmental projects meet industry standards and regulatory requirements.

As a Field Technician I, you will work alongside experienced professionals, gaining practical field experience, developing technical skills, and contributing to critical projects that impact communities. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, safety-conscious, and thrives in outdoor work environments, solving challenges in real time and collaborating with a team. This position requires frequent travel to job sites and offers excellent opportunities for growth, technical training, and career advancement in a dynamic industry.

To learn more about the important work our Field Technicians perform, here’s a short video: UES Field Technician

Responsibilities

Conduct field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and other construction materials to verify compliance with project specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Properly collect, label, and transport samples from job sites to laboratories for further testing and analysis.
Ensure that project testing requirements are met and compliant with project specifications, requirements, and company policies or procedures.
Complete detailed reports, logs, and documentation of test results, ensuring accuracy and timely submission to project managers and stakeholders.
Ensure all testing equipment is properly maintained, and functioning correctly, following company and manufacturer guidelines.
Accurately document test results, observations, and site conditions, preparing and submitting timely and detailed reports, logs, and presentations in accordance with company standards.
Communicate effectively with dispatch, field supervisors, contractors, and project managers, providing real-time updates on job status, site conditions, and any issues encountered.
Adhere to project timelines and schedules, reporting to job sites on time and completing assignments within established deadlines.
Adapt to changing project requirements, schedules, and weather conditions, maintaining flexibility to support business needs.
Participate in ongoing training and certification programs, as required, to maintain technical proficiency and industry compliance.
Follow strict safety protocols and OSHA regulations to maintain a safe work environment, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to company and client safety guidelines.
Operate and maintain an assigned company vehicle, including scheduling routine maintenance (oil changes, tire checks, fluid levels) and ensuring general cleanliness inside and out.
Perform other duties as assigned to support project goals and company initiatives.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; vocational training or coursework in construction, engineering, geology, or a related field is a plus.
0-3 years of experience in a field-based, outdoor, or physically demanding role preferred (construction, materials testing, geotechnical, or related industry experience is a plus).
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to operate company-assigned vehicles safely.
Industry certifications as applicable such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing, or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Commitment to workplace safety, following OSHA standards and company safety policies, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Basic computer proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Efficient time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate sample collection, testing procedures, and documentation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to producing high-quality results.
Flexibility to work varying schedules, including early mornings, weekends, overtime, and potential overnight travel as project demands require.

Travel Requirements

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 70% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position primarily works in an outdoor work environment, regularly exposed to varying field conditions, including:

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

The physical requirements for this position may include and are not limited to:

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.
Ability to stand, walk, drive, and operate equipment for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and arms for typing, handling tools, and operating equipment.
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, climb, balance, lift, carry, and push as required for fieldwork and inspections.
Ability to speak and hear effectively to communicate in noisy environments and with project teams.
Ability to use your senses to see (including close, distant, and peripheral vision, depth vision, and ability to focus) smell, hear, touch (use hands to reach climb or balance, crouch, stoop, crawl, kneel and sit).

jobs.description:
Overview

Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. It is at the core of how we operate and the reason for our success. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.

HYBRID:
Qualified candidates (in or near hub locations listed below) should plan to spend time working from home and some time working in the office as part of our hybrid work environment.

HUB LOCATIONS:
Richardson, TX; Bloomington, IL; Tempe, AZ; Dunwoody, GA

SPONSORSHIP: Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (e.g., H-1B visa) for this opportunity.

Responsibilities

The Experimentation team identifies the highest-value customer and business opportunities, translates them into thematic testing roadmaps, and partners with data science to ensure experiments generate trustworthy, actionable learning and measurable improvement.

Build a customer-centered growth experimentation portfolio by turning the strongest areas of need and opportunity into thematic testing roadmaps, and make sure every A/B test is designed and run to produce trustworthy, reusable learning. This role brings together conversion rate optimization (CRO), data-driven digital product management, and data-driven experience design to improve how customers move through our digital journeys. It is part of the Digital Growth Engine, a multidisciplinary organization focused on building a stronger learning advantage through trusted data, disciplined experimentation, intelligent decisioning, and scalable technology.

Identify high-value opportunity areas using customer insights, product analytics, clickstream analytics, business priorities, and journey performance.
Organize opportunities into strategic themes and maintain a sequenced experimentation roadmap based on expected value, learning potential, feasibility, and dependencies.
Write clear hypotheses that define the customer problem, intended behavior change, treatment concept, and business rationale for each experiment.
Partner with data science on test design, metrics, sample requirements, guardrails, and interpretation standards.
Coordinate with product, design, engineering, marketing, analytics, and data science to move A/B tests and multivariate experiments from concept to live experience, implemented in ways that preserve measurement integrity.

Technical proficiency in data profiling, data validation, and data storage/retrieval principles for Azure, document databases, and relational databases.

Experience with Databricks, serverless SQL, Data Governance, and Data Quality.

Experience working in Agile environments and with cloud platforms.

The Lead Electrical Power Project Coordinator
will provide senior-level field and project coordination support for the successful execution and delivery of complex mission-critical electrical power projects. This role will work cross-functionally with project management, engineering, field services, commissioning, vendors, contractors, and clients to coordinate equipment delivery, installation, QA/QC, issue resolution, and L1-L5 commissioning activities.

The Lead Electrical Power Project Coordinator will serve as a key technical resource throughout project execution, helping ensure electrical power systems and equipment are delivered, installed, tested, and commissioned safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project specifications and industry standards.

Essential Functions

Project Coordination

Support Senior Project Managers and Program Managers with project schedules, budgets, resource allocation, milestones, and progress tracking.
Coordinate day-to-day field activities associated with electrical power equipment installation and project execution.
Collaborate closely with project management, engineering, commissioning, field service, vendors, contractors, and client representatives.
Coordinate equipment deliveries, staging, installation, testing, and turnover activities.
Proactively identify project risks, schedule impacts, technical issues, and potential delays and assist in developing mitigation strategies.
Track project deliverables and communicate project status, issues, and action items to internal and external stakeholders.
Assist with coordinating multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.

Electrical Power Technical Support

Provide senior-level technical support related to mission-critical electrical power systems and equipment.
Interpret and coordinate electrical construction drawings, one-lines, equipment layouts, specifications, and project documentation.
Support installation and integration of electrical power distribution systems and equipment.
Troubleshoot technical issues and coordinate appropriate corrective actions with engineering, contractors, manufacturers, and field personnel.

Medium- and low-voltage switchgear
Switchboards and distribution equipment
UPS systems
Generators
Automatic and static transfer switches
PDUs
Transformers
Busway systems
Protective devices and controls
Critical power distribution systems

Demonstrate an understanding of data center electrical topologies, redundancy, resiliency, and critical power distribution schemes.

Inspect completed work for compliance with drawings, specifications, codes, and project requirements.
Identify deficiencies, document discrepancies, and coordinate corrective actions.
Assist with equipment production, delivery, installation, and turnover schedules.
Support integrated testing and L1-L5 commissioning activities.
Coordinate with commissioning teams, contractors, vendors, and project stakeholders to resolve commissioning issues.
Assist in maintaining project documentation, inspection records, punch lists, testing documentation, and turnover packages.

Identify potential safety hazards and communicate concerns to appropriate project and field leadership.
Support safe execution of electrical installation, testing, commissioning, and field activities.

Minimum of 5 years of field and/or project experience in electrical construction, electrical power systems, mission-critical facilities, data centers, commissioning, or related environments.
Strong electrical background; journeyman or master's electrical license is a plus.
Demonstrated experience coordinating complex electrical power projects and field activities.
Strong understanding of electrical construction drawings, one-lines, equipment layouts, specifications, and project documentation.
Strong understanding of mission-critical electrical power distribution systems and equipment, including switchgear, generators, UPS, PDU, STS, ATS, transformers, and related equipment.

Experience working with electrical contractors, equipment manufacturers, engineering firms, commissioning agents, and project management teams.

Advanced proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, Outlook, and PowerPoint.

Strong project coordination, organizational, and time-management skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple projects, priorities, and deadlines simultaneously.
Strong leadership and interpersonal skills with the ability to lead, collaborate, motivate, and support cross-functional teams.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Ability to communicate effectively with clients, contractors, vendors, engineers, project managers, and field personnel.
Ability to work independently while maintaining strong coordination with project leadership.
Professionalism, discretion, and the ability to maintain confidentiality.

Through the integration of its hospitals, labs, and schools, Mount Sinai offers comprehensive health care solutions from birth through geriatrics, leveraging innovative approaches such as artificial intelligence and informatics while keeping patients’ medical and emotional needs at the center of all treatment. The Health System includes more than 9,000 primary and specialty care physicians; 13 joint-venture outpatient surgery centers throughout the five boroughs of New York City, Westchester, Long Island, and Florida; and more than 30 affiliated community health centers. We are consistently ranked by U.S. News & World Report's Best Hospitals, receiving high "Honor Roll" status, and are highly ranked: No. 1 in Geriatrics, top 5 in Cardiology/Heart Surgery, and top 20 in Diabetes/Endocrinology, Gastroenterology/GI Surgery, Neurology/Neurosurgery, Orthopedics, Pulmonology/Lung Surgery, Rehabilitation, and Urology. New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai is ranked No. 12 in Ophthalmology. U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Children’s Hospitals” ranks Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital among the country’s best in several pediatric specialties. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is ranked No. 11 nationwide in National Institutes of Health funding and in the 99th percentile in research dollars per investigator according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. Newsweek’s “The World’s Best Smart Hospitals” ranks The Mount Sinai Hospital as No. 1 in New York and in the top five globally, and Mount Sinai Morningside in the top 20 globally.

and

As a top-10 engineering school with the No. 1 program in Texas, the Cockrell School of Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) has been a global leader in technology innovation and engineering education for over a century. With 11 undergraduate and 13 graduate programs, over 20 research centers and a faculty community that boasts one of the highest number of National Academy of Engineering members among U.S. universities, Texas Engineering has launched some of the nation’s most accomplished leaders and pioneered world-changing solutions in virtually every industry, from space exploration to energy to health care. Situated in the heart of Austin — named “America’s Coolest City” by Expedia and “The Best Place to Live in the U.S.” by U.S. News and World Report — the Cockrell School embodies the city’s innovative spirit. Major companies with Austin campuses, such as Dell, National Instruments, Apple, IBM, Samsung, Google and many others, continue to recruit Cockrell School students at a remarkable rate, launching thousands of successful careers and developing Texas Engineers into industry leaders.

At UT Austin, we say “What starts here changes the world.” As a member of the university community, you will be part of an organization that is internationally recognized for our academic programs and research. Your work will have meaning and make a difference not only in the lives of our faculty, staff, and students, but also those who are impacted by our first-class academic and research programs.

Based at the Cockrell School of Engineering at UT Austin, the Construction Industry Institute (CII) is the premier research & development platform for the capital projects industry. Department Information
Are you interested in making a difference in the lives of fellow Californians while achieving your career goals? Do you set high standards for yourself and enjoy a collaborative and challenging work environment? The mission of the California Department of Social Services is to serve, protect, and support the people of California experiencing need in ways that empower wellbeing and disrupt systemic inequities. The vision of the California Department of Social Services is to provide quality services with a commitment to an inclusive, diverse, and equitable California where all people can thrive.

The Research, Automation, and Data Division’s (RADDs) mission is to improve the way the Department collects, manages, and deploys data to support the efficient, effective, and equitable delivery of government social services. RADD manages major statewide initiatives to streamline and automate eligibility determination and benefit administration for key safety net programs, and leads efforts such as human-centered design, data governance, automation and continuous quality improvement, data visualization and analysis, and research partnerships to improve client outcomes and promote program integrity. Across these efforts, RADD provides coaching to the Department on all aspects of the data lifecycle.

CDSS Guiding Principles

Diversity. Equity. Inclusion. Accessibility. Belonging.
We ensure opportunities for everyone to participate in a meaningful way in fulfilling the mission and vision of CDSS.

Community Engagement
We prioritize the lived experiences of community members as a driving force behind the creation, implementation, desired impact, or change of programs and services.

Empowerment
We engage, operate, and advocate from the understanding that each community and person have desires and capabilities to lead in their own life.

Quality Services
We provide services that align intent and impact by ensuring that they are accessible, community driven, interconnected, and continuously improved.

Data Defined Outcomes
We equitably collect and analyze data, take data-driven action, and measure outcomes relevant to those we serve, ensuring transparency and accountability.

Job Description And Duties
Are you ready to champion data that drives real change for California families? Join the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) as a Research Data Specialist II, where you’ll transform raw data into accurate, timely data products that influence policy decisions, support budget development, and inform how counties deliver critical services. As part of the Research, Automation & Data Division (RADD), and the Research & Data Insights (RDI) Branch, you will contribute to CDSS’s mission of building a sustainable, data-driven culture. You’ll play a pivotal role in producing accurate data required for State and Federal reporting, supporting program partners, and improving outcomes for vulnerable families statewide.

What You’ll Do

Serve as a technical lead for advanced data engineering, data management, and statistical analysis across major social service programs including child welfare, Temporary Aid for Needy Families (TANF), and the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
Build and maintain complex reporting pipelines in Snowflake, extracting, validating, and reconciling data from multiple systems to meet detailed State and Federal reporting requirements. Produce compliant, audit-ready reporting files with robust documentation of methodologies and transformations.
Develop original statistical programming and analytical code using SQL (Snowflake), Python, and R. Design reusable datasets, views, and stored procedures; perform sophisticated joins, window functions, and semi-structured data processing. Produce high-quality insights for program oversight, evaluation, and policy development.
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to Research Data Analysts II and Research Data Specialists I, supporting skill development in coding, analytics, and reporting standards. Lead limited-term projects with teams of up to six researchers.

Why Join Us?

Play a key role in building CDSS’s modern, statewide data ecosystem.
Influence high-visibility reporting and analytical work that shapes policy and funding decisions affecting millions.
Collaborate in a mission-driven environment that values innovation, transparency, and human-centered design.
Grow your technical and leadership impact while helping California deliver better services to its most vulnerable populations.

The Department of Social Services does not participate in E-Verify for employment authorization purposes. Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States without the need for visa sponsorship by the start date of employment.

If you would like to share how you learned about this career opportunity, please take a moment to complete our brief Recruitment Survey.

Need help with applying for positions, taking an examination, or preparing for interviews? Our team is here to support you, reach out anytime at Recruiter@dss.ca.gov . For guidance on applying for a state job, visit Three Steps to a State Job

Follow us on LinkedIn to stay updated on our latest opportunities.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Special Requirements

Please Note:
A Statement of Qualifications or Supplemental Questionnaire must be submitted along with your application to be considered for this position. Applications submitted without an SOQ may be disqualified for this position.

Do not
include any confidential information in any documents (i.e., application, resume, or transcripts) you submit for this job vacancy. Confidential information that should be excluded or removed from these documents include but is not limited to: Social Security Number (SSN), birthday and/or age, photos, student/other ID number, driver’s license number (unless required), basis of eligibility, exam results, LEAP status, and marital status. Confidential information submitted via a CalCareer Account (electronic application) is automatically redacted upon submission.

The SOQ must be submitted along with the Application/Standard Form (STD) 678 in CalCareers. The SOQ should be typed, with a length of approximately one page, at Arial 12 pt. font. The response should be no more than 500 words. Application packages received without specific responses to the supplemental questionnaire will not be considered.

Your SOQ must specifically address the following questions to be considered for this position:

Please describe how your education, training, experience and skills make you an ideal candidate for this position.
Describe your experience creating data-processing workflows in a cloud data environment (such as Snowflake). Provide an example of a process you built or improved, the tools you used, and how you made sure the data was accurate and met required standards.
Describe your experience leading analytical or data-focused projects and collaborating with cross-functional teams. Include an example of how you guided or supported other analysts, coordinated with program or technical partners, and helped ensure the success of a shared project or data initiative.

new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

INTERA is seeking a Geologist / Hydrogeologist / Geophysicist for our Austin office to support groundwater, water supply, environmental, and subsurface characterization projects throughout Texas and the western United States. This is a primarily desktop-based role centered on data interpretation, modeling, analysis, and technical reporting rather than field work. The role suits an early- to mid-career professional with 2–5 years of applied experience in geology, hydrogeology, geophysics, petrophysics, geological or petroleum engineering, environmental consulting, or a related subsurface discipline who wants to broaden their technical expertise alongside experienced practitioners in these fields.

Key Responsibilities

Subsurface Characterization and Interpretation

Interpret borehole geophysical logs (gamma ray, spontaneous potential, resistivity, density, neutron, sonic, acoustic, and caliper) and petrophysical datasets to evaluate lithology, porosity, permeability, fracture occurrence, aquifer and production-zone properties, water-quality indicators, and subsurface heterogeneity.
Develop and calibrate petrophysical models from borehole geophysical log data for geologic property characterization, groundwater quality estimations, and environmental investigations.
Interpret geologic, hydrostratigraphic, and structural relationships from borehole logs, geologic maps, and geophysical data; characterize alluvial, sedimentary, carbonate, fractured-rock, and mixed aquifer systems; and identify hydrostratigraphic units, aquifer boundaries, and groundwater-quality trends.
Develop cross sections, hydrostratigraphic frameworks, fence diagrams, and conceptual site and digital subsurface models, integrating borehole logs, core and laboratory analyses, drilling data, geophysical surveys, and aquifer testing and monitoring results into defensible interpretations and recommendations.
Support well siting, well design, and aquifer characterization through geologic, geophysical, and petrophysical analysis.

Groundwater Studies and Numerical Modeling

Support groundwater resource evaluations, water supply development studies, and aquifer characterization projects.
Compile and interpret groundwater level, pumping, aquifer test, recharge, and water-quality datasets to assess aquifer properties, groundwater availability, well performance, and sustainability.
Support development of hydrogeologic conceptual models used for water resource planning, groundwater management, and environmental investigations.
Support the groundwater modeling team with the development, calibration, and interpretation of groundwater flow, contaminant transport, subsidence, and subsurface process models using finite difference, finite element, or related numerical techniques.
Assist with sensitivity analyses, history matching, uncertainty evaluations, and predictive simulations, and prepare summaries that communicate model assumptions, results, and limitations.

Data Analysis, GIS, and Workflows

Manage, analyze, and visualize subsurface and water-quality datasets, applying quantitative, statistical, and machine-learning methods to evaluate trends and support predictive modeling.
Develop maps, cross sections, dashboards, and figures to communicate project findings, using GIS software for spatial analysis and data management.
Develop automated, reproducible workflows for interpretation, visualization, and analysis using Python, MATLAB, or similar tools.

Reporting and Communication

Prepare technical memoranda, reports, figures, and presentations, and clearly communicate findings to project teams, clients, regulators, and stakeholders.
Support proposals, work plans, cost estimates, and deliverables, and participate in technical reviews and quality assurance/quality control.

Requirements

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Geology, Hydrogeology, Geological Engineering, Geophysics, Environmental Science, or a closely related field.
2–5 years of professional or graduate-level experience in hydrogeology, geology, groundwater investigations, geophysical interpretation, environmental consulting, or subsurface characterization.
Experience evaluating and interpreting complex subsurface and water-quality datasets, including borehole geophysical logs and petrophysical interpretation, to characterize subsurface systems and support technical decision-making.
Understanding of hydrogeologic principles including groundwater flow, aquifer characterization, recharge, aquifer testing, and water supply development, and experience developing cross sections, hydrostratigraphic frameworks, and conceptual site models.
Working knowledge of subsurface-based geophysical investigation and interpretation methods, including borehole logging and 2D/3D seismic.
Experience using Python, MATLAB, or similar scientific computing tools, and ArcGIS Pro and/or QGIS, for data analysis, visualization, automation, modeling, and spatial analysis.
Strong quantitative, analytical, technical writing, and communication skills, with the ability to work independently and within multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Professional Geologist (PG) license, or ability to obtain licensure within a reasonable timeframe.
Master's degree or PhD in Geology, Hydrogeology, Geophysics, Geological Engineering, Petroleum Engineering, or a closely related discipline.
Experience supporting groundwater supply development, well siting, aquifer storage and recovery (ASR), groundwater management, or water resource planning projects.
Experience interpreting borehole geophysical logs, applying petrophysical methods, and integrating subsurface, groundwater chemistry, and water-quality datasets into conceptual site models.
Familiarity with groundwater flow modeling and MODFLOW-based models, numerical simulation, porous-media flow, or reservoir characterization.
Proficiency with Python, MATLAB, or similar languages, and with PETRA, Leapfrog, ArcGIS Pro, Techlog, Interactive Petrophysics (IP), Petrel, or similar interpretation and modeling software.
Experience interpreting laboratory, core analysis, and petrophysical measurement data, and supporting environmental remediation, energy, geothermal, mining, carbon management, subsurface storage, or water-resource development projects, including proposal preparation and client interaction.

Required

Bachelor's degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or related environmental discipline. Minimum 3.0 GPA, or equivalent experience.
1-2 years of experience.
Willingness and interest in field assignments; ability to perform field work standing or walking for full field days.
Strong commitment to safety, including following established Health and Safety protocols.
Effective written and verbal communication skills along with strong organizational and analytical abilities.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Detail-oriented with a solutions-focused, results-oriented approach and strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

Ability to lift at least 40 pounds.
Driver's License Required: This position requires a valid driver's license and/or the ability to operate a company vehicle due to the nature of job duties, which include frequent travel to various client locations across a large geographical area.

Preferred

Master's degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, environmental science, or related environmental discipline.
Experience recording and writing detailed technical data and reports.
40-hour OSHA HAZWOPER certification.
GIT or EIT certification.
Local candidates preferred.

Conduct field work, including data collection; soil, sediment, groundwater, surface water, soil vapor, and indoor air sampling; aquifer testing; drilling oversight and soil logging; soil boring and monitoring well installation; well development, purging and sampling; remedial and wastewater treatment pilot tests; remedial system operation and maintenance; and in-plant support.

Compile and evaluate data and assist in report preparation.

Work within quality, budget, schedule expectations, and scope-specific assignments.
Communicate with subcontractors, regulatory agents, tenants, and clients during field activities.

for our Savannah, GA

Assist with Phase I and Phase II Environmental Site Assessments, site reconnaissance, and environmental due diligence activities.
Conduct field investigations, including soil, groundwater, surface water, sediment, soil vapor, and air sampling.
Support installation, development, and sampling of monitoring wells and other environmental investigation points.

Coordinate with subcontractors, laboratories, drillers, and internal project teams to support safe and efficient field execution.
Assist with data review, interpretation of analytical results, preparation of tables and figures, and development of technical reports.
Support remediation activities, including excavation oversight, groundwater monitoring, remedial system operation and maintenance, and confirmation sampling.
Follow company and client health and safety requirements, including preparation for field work and participation in job safety briefings.
Maintain equipment, manage supplies, and support project logistics for field assignments.
Work collaboratively with multidisciplinary teams to deliver high-quality environmental consulting services.
Undertake project-based travel and site work, both within the United States and internationally. The frequency and duration of project-based travel will depend on business and client needs.
Complete training on assigned tasks.
Exercise responsible and ethical decision-making regarding company funds, resources and conduct, and adhere to WSP’s Code of Conduct and related policies and procedures.
Perform additional responsibilities as required by business needs.

Who You Are

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, or closely related discipline.
The ability to obtain professional licensure (EIT/ PE).
0 to 1 years of relevant experience in environmental consulting, field investigation, remediation, or a related technical field.
Strong interest in site investigation, environmental sampling, remediation, and regulatory compliance.
Ability to perform field work in varying weather conditions and site environments.
Ability to operate, troubleshoot, and maintain field testing and monitoring equipment.
Ability to lift and transport a minimum of 50 pounds on a regular basis during the course of field work.
Valid driver’s license and ability to safely operate a motor vehicle on behalf of the company to travel locally or regionally for field assignments.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with attention to detail in documentation and reporting.
Basic proficiency with technical writing, office automation and communication software, technology, and tools.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team while managing multiple priorities.

Ability to work schedules conducive to project-specific requirements that may extend beyond the typical workweek.
Willingness to travel for field work as dictated by project demands, which could be as much as 75% of the time and to periodically adjust personal schedules to meet project needs.
The selected candidate must have the ability to work in the United States immediately.
Must be able to pass a HAZWOPER physical and be medically able to wear a tight-fitting respirator / Fit for Duty Exam / Medical Exam.

40-Hour OSHA Health & Safety Training (HAZWOPER) (29 CFR 1910.120)
Experience performing soil and rock logging.
Experience performing soil, sediment, soil gas, and/or groundwater sampling.
Familiarity with various drilling techniques and experience with installation of groundwater monitoring and/or remediation wells.
Experience with software such as AutoCAD, ArcGIS, EQuIS, OpenGround, Rockworks, EVS, and/or Leapfrog a plus.
Experience with groundwater and plume modeling software, such as Surfer, MODFLOW, MODPATH, and/or MT3DMS, and associated interface/processing packages, such as Groundwater Vistas.
A member of and/or actively participate in local professional practice organizations.

WSP USA is the U.S. operating company of WSP, one of the world's leading engineering and professional services firms. . In this position, you will contribute to innovative and challenging environmental projects, including the financial and technical evaluation, detailed design, permitting, and construction stages, while further developing the business skills needed for a successful consulting career.

new_jobs.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

INTERA Incorporated is seeking a senior-level Geologist and Drilling Coordinator to join its Mining and Environmental Line of Business in the Albuquerque, New Mexico office. This role leads drilling-based field events for a variety of reclamation, remediation, and environmental characterization projects. The position also supports clients in meeting regulatory requirements, restoring impacted sites, and sustainably managing natural resources.

This position will include implementing highly technical work plans for complex projects, serving as the primary link between field operations and the project manager while leading teams of personnel to conduct field and office support work for subsurface contamination investigations, geotechnical studies, groundwater monitoring well installation and development, etc. Clients include state and municipal agencies and private industries that share our values of environmental stewardship and technical excellence.

Key Responsibilities

Lead daily site activities, manage field crews, and oversee work performed by drilling contractors and subcontractors to ensure work is completed in accordance with workplans, design drawings, specifications, and client expectations.
Ensure compliance with health and safety requirements for fieldwork.
Collect environmental samples (soil/rock, aqueous, vapor), oversee drilling soil borings and monitoring well installation, and conduct hydraulic testing.
Ensure accuracy of drilling data and submit status reports to the Project Manager.
Develop cost estimates and proposals for drilling projects, including acquiring bids from multiple drilling firms and other vendors while ensuring consistency between and amongst the bids.
Plan drilling programs including resource and equipment needs, preparation of field implementation plans that reference standard operation procedures (SOPs), sampling and analysis plans, and Health and Safety plans.
Work with colleagues to ensure that the selected drilling contractor is aware of, and complies with, INTERA Statements of Work; including drilling type/style, schedule/forecast, oversight and review of drilling tickets, lithologic interpretation, geophysical logging, well construction, post-construction development, pump design and placement, aquifer testing, permanent pump design and placement, and all equipment associated with remote monitoring of the well/wellfield.
Log soil and rock core utilizing ASTM standards for lithologic interpretation and prepare boring logs.
Analyze environmental data and author detailed technical reports.
Participate in environmental site characterization investigations, including soil gas investigations, soil sampling, and groundwater sampling.
Continue to build upon and refine INTERA’s approach to drilling operations, including updating SOP’s and identifying potential inefficiencies.
Mentor junior staff and collaborate with technical teams across the company.
Support business development by maintaining client relationships and identifying new opportunities. Maintain regular contact with an ever-increasing list of drillers and related contractors.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, or related field.
10+ years of relevant professional experience with increasing levels of responsibility.
Professional licensure or willingness to obtain.
Proficiency in various borehole advancement methods, including but not limited to sonic, hollow stem auger, direct push, air rotary casing hammer, and flooded reverse circulation mud rotary.
Demonstrated experience managing drilling projects.
Strong leadership, technical report writing, problem-solving, and verbal communication skills with the ability to convey complex thoughts and ideas in a clear and concise manner.
General knowledge of hydrogeology, nature, and extent of contamination evaluation.
The ability to work with a project team or independently to complete technical work.
Experience developing and maintaining long-lasting relationships with drilling firms.
Experience analyzing geophysical logs.
Willingness to travel to project sites (50% - 70%) and other INTERA offices (primarily within New Mexico and Texas).

Preferred Qualifications

Master’s degree in geology, hydrogeology, engineering, or related field.
Familiarity with state and federal environmental regulations (e.g., RCRA, CERCLA, NMED/NMAC, OSE, EPA) and risk-based criteria.
Proficiency in various environmental sampling techniques such as heated head space soil sampling, soil sampling, push-ahead groundwater sampling, and zonal groundwater sampling.
Experience with pLog and Logplot software.
Previous experience with aquifer test (Aqtesolv, nSIGHTS) and geologic modeling software (Leapfrog preferred)
OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER Certification

About INTERA & Our Benefits

INTERA is a Top Workplaces USA 2025 award winner!

Founded In 1974, INTERA Has Grown Into An International Geosciences And Engineering Consulting Firm That Helps Clients Make Informed Business Decisions, Mitigate Risk, And Drive Optimal Outcomes In a Multitude Of Industries. We Strive To Foster An Environment Where People Love The Work That They Do And The Place That They Work Because We Believe That Our Employees Are Our Most Valuable Asset. Paid parental leave – up to 12 weeks for birthing and non-birthing parents
Group term life and accidental death and dismemberment insurance, short-term and long-term coverage – paid 100% by the company

Opportunities for stock ownership

Tuition reimbursement, financial assistance for professional licensure and registration, and one paid membership to a professional society

Company Description

The Vertex Companies, LLC (Vertex) is a $180M global consulting firm that integrates strategic advisory, project management, and dispute resolution services for organizations facing complex challenges in a world of risk. We embody our core values of embracing lifelong learning, operating with urgency, maximizing value, and driving collaboration to better outcomes for our clients, colleagues, and communities. Join us if you are looking for a career that offers you a chance to love what you do and deliver meaningful impact.

Job Description

The Geologist will conduct Phase 1 and Phase II Assessments for our clients. Frequent travel to our client's project locations across the region is required. This role will require frequent travel in the Houston TX area.

Core Responsibilities

Work Product Creation, Project Management, Coordination with Team Members

Conduct Phase I Environmental Site Assessments (ESAs) and Phase II Subsurface Investigations in accordance with applicable regulatory and industry standards.
Perform site reconnaissance and field evaluations for Phase I ESAs, Phase II investigations, and related environmental due diligence assignments.
Oversee environmental drilling and sampling activities, including subcontractor coordination, soil logging, groundwater sampling, field documentation, and communication with project stakeholders.
Prepare high-quality, client-facing technical reports, including environmental assessment findings, analytical data summaries, figures, tables, and recommendations.
Develop proposals, scopes of work, and cost estimates for environmental assessment, investigation, and remediation projects.
Support contaminated site characterization and remediation programs through field implementation, data evaluation, and reporting.
Perform construction observation and related environmental field services, as required.

Operations

Coordinate project activities with senior managers to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, on schedule, and within budget.
Assist in monitoring project milestones, budgets, schedules, and other key performance indicators.
Support the selection, coordination, and management of project team members, subcontractors, and specialty consultants.
Prepare and implement site-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs) and Job Safety Analyses (JSAs) to maintain regulatory compliance and safe work practices.
Maintain effective communication with clients, project teams, subcontractors, and regulatory stakeholders throughout project execution.
Manage multiple assignments simultaneously while maintaining quality standards and meeting established deadlines.
Participate in frequent travel and field assignments to support project execution across various geographic locations.

Qualifications & Competencies

Bachelor’s degree and a minimum of 2 years of related experience; or an advanced degree without experience; or 5 years of related work experience and no degree.
Demonstrated experience conducting ASTM Phase I Environmental Site Assessments and Phase II subsurface investigations.
Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage competing priorities and deadlines.
Excellent verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Proven ability to work independently in the field and collaboratively within multidisciplinary project teams.
Detail-oriented with a commitment to technical accuracy, quality, and client service.
Ability and willingness to travel frequently for field assignments; valid driver's license required.

Knowledge & Skills

Working knowledge of ASTM environmental assessment standards and industry best practices.
Understanding of environmental site characterization, contaminated site investigation, and remediation principles.
Strong technical writing and documentation skills, including preparation of environmental reports and deliverables.
Experience with environmental sampling methodologies, soil logging, groundwater monitoring, and data interpretation.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook).
Familiarity with AutoCAD, Geographic Information Systems (GIS), or similar technical software is preferred.
Knowledge of environmental health and safety protocols, including development and implementation of HASPs and JSAs.
Ability to analyze technical data and present findings clearly to clients and project stakeholders.

new_jobs.title: Field Technician I
new_jobs.description:
Overview

At UES, we’re a team of more than 4,000 engineers, scientists, geologists, inspectors, technicians, and drillers united by a shared purpose—to make a meaningful impact in the communities we serve. As a national leader in geotechnical engineering, environmental consulting, and materials testing and inspection, we collaborate on transformative projects across transportation, energy, water, healthcare, and more. Learn more about the benefits of joining Team UES and our core values at careers.teamues.com.

Position Overview

We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Field Technician I to join our team and support engineering, environmental services, materials testing, and inspection projects. In this role, you will conduct on-site inspections, materials testing, and environmental sampling to ensure construction, infrastructure, and environmental projects meet industry standards and regulatory requirements.

As a Field Technician I, you will work alongside experienced professionals, gaining practical field experience, developing technical skills, and contributing to critical projects that impact communities. The ideal candidate is detail-oriented, safety-conscious, and thrives in outdoor work environments, solving challenges in real time and collaborating with a team. This position requires frequent travel to job sites and offers excellent opportunities for growth, technical training, and career advancement in a dynamic industry.

To learn more about the important work our Field Technicians perform, here’s a short video: UES Field Technician

Responsibilities

Conduct field and laboratory testing of soil, concrete, asphalt, aggregate, and other construction materials to verify compliance with project specifications, industry standards, and regulatory requirements.
Properly collect, label, and transport samples from job sites to laboratories for further testing and analysis.
Ensure that project testing requirements are met and compliant with project specifications, requirements, and company policies or procedures.
Complete detailed reports, logs, and documentation of test results, ensuring accuracy and timely submission to project managers and stakeholders.
Ensure all testing equipment is properly maintained, and functioning correctly, following company and manufacturer guidelines.
Accurately document test results, observations, and site conditions, preparing and submitting timely and detailed reports, logs, and presentations in accordance with company standards.
Communicate effectively with dispatch, field supervisors, contractors, and project managers, providing real-time updates on job status, site conditions, and any issues encountered.
Adhere to project timelines and schedules, reporting to job sites on time and completing assignments within established deadlines.
Adapt to changing project requirements, schedules, and weather conditions, maintaining flexibility to support business needs.
Participate in ongoing training and certification programs, as required, to maintain technical proficiency and industry compliance.
Follow strict safety protocols and OSHA regulations to maintain a safe work environment, including proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE) and adherence to company and client safety guidelines.
Operate and maintain an assigned company vehicle, including scheduling routine maintenance (oil changes, tire checks, fluid levels) and ensuring general cleanliness inside and out.
Perform other duties as assigned to support project goals and company initiatives.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required; vocational training or coursework in construction, engineering, geology, or a related field is a plus.
0-3 years of experience in a field-based, outdoor, or physically demanding role preferred (construction, materials testing, geotechnical, or related industry experience is a plus).
Valid driver’s license with an acceptable driving record; ability to operate company-assigned vehicles safely.
Industry certifications as applicable such as ACI Level 1 Concrete Testing, or ability to obtain within a specified time period.
Commitment to workplace safety, following OSHA standards and company safety policies, including the proper use of personal protective equipment (PPE).
Basic computer proficiency, including experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook) and Field Data Collection (FDC) software or similar industry tools.
Mathematical skills sufficient to add, subtract, multiply, and divide into all units of measure using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
Ability to read, write, and interpret blueprints, procedures, manuals, technical documents, and reports related to drilling, safety, and project requirements.
Efficient time management, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to complete tasks efficiently and accurately.
Attention to detail to ensure accurate sample collection, testing procedures, and documentation.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively, demonstrating a strong work ethic and commitment to producing high-quality results.
Flexibility to work varying schedules, including early mornings, weekends, overtime, and potential overnight travel as project demands require.

Travel Requirements

This position requires extensive travel, approximately up to 70% of the time, in support of business

objectives and client engagements. Travel may be both scheduled and on short notice, depending on

project needs. Destinations typically include job sites, field locations, or regional offices, where work may be conducted in outdoor or operational environments. Adherence to all company safety protocols and use of PPE is required during travel and on-site work.

Physical Demands & Work Environment

This position primarily works in an outdoor work environment, regularly exposed to varying field conditions, including:

Sites that may not be accessible by vehicle, requiring travel on foot through wetlands, swamps, grasslands, fields, and other uneven or rugged terrain with natural and man-made obstacles such as sand, brush, and debris.
Moderate to loud noise levels, common in active construction and industrial environments.
Exposure to environmental elements including dirt, dust, sun, heat, humidity, and adverse weather conditions.

The physical requirements for this position may include and are not limited to:

Ability to lift and/or carry 35 to 50 lbs. up to 75 feet, involving regular repetitive motion.
Ability to stand, walk, drive, and operate equipment for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and arms for typing, handling tools, and operating equipment.
Ability to bend, twist, reach, stoop, pull, kneel, climb, balance, lift, carry, and push as required for fieldwork and inspections.

Build a customer-centered growth experimentation portfolio by turning the strongest areas of need and opportunity into thematic testing roadmaps, and make sure every A/B test is designed and run to produce trustworthy, reusable learning. Quality and value of the opportunity portfolio and strategic recommendations.

Stakeholder alignment and evidence that learning turns into scaled action.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-ready storytelling and decision support.
