new_jobs.title: Data Analyst - Strategist, Digital Experimentation & Analytics
new_jobs.description:
Overview

Being good neighbors – helping people, investing in our communities, and making the world a better place – is who we are at State Farm. It is at the core of how we operate and the reason for our success. We're moving with urgency to become a Next Gen Good Neighbor, with technology that strengthens human connections and enhances the customer experience. As an employee, you'll spend less time navigating systems and more time applying judgment, empathy, and expertise in the moments that matter most.

HYBRID:
Qualified candidates (in or near hub locations listed below) should plan to spend time working from home and some time working in the office as part of our hybrid work environment.

HUB LOCATIONS:
Richardson, TX; Bloomington, IL; Tempe, AZ; Dunwoody, GA

SPONSORSHIP: Applicants are required to be eligible to lawfully work in the U.S. immediately; employer will not sponsor applicants for U.S. work authorization (e.g., H-1B visa) for this opportunity.

Responsibilities

The Experimentation team identifies the highest-value customer and business opportunities, translates them into thematic testing roadmaps, and partners with data science to ensure experiments generate trustworthy, actionable learning and measurable improvement.

Build a customer-centered growth experimentation portfolio by turning the strongest areas of need and opportunity into thematic testing roadmaps, and make sure every A/B test is designed and run to produce trustworthy, reusable learning. This role brings together conversion rate optimization (CRO), data-driven digital product management, and data-driven experience design to improve how customers move through our digital journeys. It is part of the Digital Growth Engine, a multidisciplinary organization focused on building a stronger learning advantage through trusted data, disciplined experimentation, intelligent decisioning, and scalable technology.

Identify high-value opportunity areas using customer insights, product analytics, clickstream analytics, business priorities, and journey performance.
Organize opportunities into strategic themes and maintain a sequenced experimentation roadmap based on expected value, learning potential, feasibility, and dependencies.
Write clear hypotheses that define the customer problem, intended behavior change, treatment concept, and business rationale for each experiment.
Partner with data science on test design, metrics, sample requirements, guardrails, and interpretation standards.
Coordinate with product, design, engineering, marketing, analytics, and data science to move A/B tests and multivariate experiments from concept to live experience, implemented in ways that preserve measurement integrity.
Drive CRO across key digital journeys, using behavioral data to find friction and prioritize the changes most likely to move conversion and customer outcomes.
Lead portfolio learning reviews that connect individual test results to broader themes and determine what to scale, iterate, or test next.
Identify recurring process, measurement, or data gaps and shape capability improvements that increase experimentation speed and rigor.
Communicate the experimentation pipeline, experimentation velocity, and realized value to senior stakeholders.

How Success Will Be Measured

Quality and value of the opportunity portfolio and strategic recommendations.
Speed at which ambiguous opportunities become testable, measurable decisions.
Share of experiments that launch clean and produce a readable, decision-ready result.
Stakeholder alignment and evidence that learning turns into scaled action.

Leadership & Ways of Working

Champion a test-and-learn culture, treating every experiment, including the ones that don't win, as a chance to build shared knowledge.
Put customer needs and measurable outcomes at the center of decisions.
Work with confident humility: bring expertise, invite challenge, and adapt as evidence changes.
Create clarity in ambiguity and make tradeoffs visible so teams can move with appropriate speed.
Build strong partnerships across business and technology boundaries and share learning broadly.
Operate with high standards for data stewardship, privacy, security, ethics, and enterprise risk management.

Qualifications

Experience in strategy, digital product, analytics, growth, innovation, consulting, or a related discipline.
Hands-on experience planning, running, or scaling A/B testing or growth experimentation programs, with enough statistical fluency to partner with data scientists as a peer.
Experience using Adobe Analytics or similar platforms to analyze clickstream and behavioral data and turn it into testable hypotheses.
Experience with Optimizely or a comparable experimentation platform.
Demonstrated ability to structure ambiguous problems, synthesize quantitative and qualitative evidence, and develop clear recommendations.
Strong business acumen and ability to connect customer needs, operational realities, technology capabilities, and enterprise priorities.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including executive-ready storytelling and decision support.
Ability to lead through influence and coordinate work across multidisciplinary teams in a complex enterprise environment.

Preferred Experience

Experience working in a large, regulated enterprise and navigating privacy, security, legal, risk, and governance requirements.
Experience with data-driven digital product management or experience design, ideally in insurance, financial services, or another regulated industry.
Experience with digital customer journeys, growth analytics, personalization, or marketing technology.
Demonstrated success in cross-functional product or pod-based operating models, moving work from insight to implementation.
A bias toward measurable outcomes, reusable capabilities, clear documentation, and continuous learning.

Our Benefits

Because work-life balance is a priority at State Farm, compensation is based on our standard 38:45-hour work week!

Potential starting salary range: $97,000 - $160,000
Starting salary will be based on skills, background, and experience
High end of the range limited to applicants with significant relevant experience

Potential yearly incentive pay up to 15% of base salary

At State Farm, we offer more than just a paycheck. Check out our suite of benefits designed to give you the flexibility you need to take care of you and your family!

Get Paid! On top of our competitive pay, you are eligible for an annual raise and bonus.
Stay Well! Focus on you and your family’s health with our robust health and wellbeing programs. State Farm pays most of your healthcare premium, and we offer multiple healthcare plan options, including a high deductible plan. All medical plans provide 100% coverage for in-network preventative care, AND you and your family have access to vision, dental, telemedicine, 24/7 mental health professionals, and much more!
Develop and Grow! Take advantage of educational benefits like industry leading training programs, top-notch tuition assistance programs, employee resource groups, and mentoring.
Plan Ahead! Plan for those big moments in life with benefits like fertility/IVF/adoption assistance, college coaching, national discount programs, interactive monthly financial workshops, free financial coaching, and more. You can also start a savings account or consider financing through our State Farm Federal Credit Union!
Take a Little “You” Time! You will have access to our generous time off policies designed so you can plan around holidays, family events, volunteering, or just to take a relaxing day off. With the opportunity to initially earn up to 20 days annually plus parental leave, paid holidays, celebration day, life leave (40 hours/year), bereavement leave, and community service/education support days, there will be plenty of time for you!
Give Back! We offer several ways to give back through our Matching Gift Program, Good Neighbor Grant Program, and the Employee Assistance Fund.
Finish Strong! Plan for retirement using free financial advisors and a 401(k) plan with company contributions of up to 7% of your salary.

The Lead Electrical Power Project Coordinator will serve as a key technical resource throughout project execution, helping ensure electrical power systems and equipment are delivered, installed, tested, and commissioned safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project specifications and industry standards.

Project Coordination

Support Senior Project Managers and Program Managers with project schedules, budgets, resource allocation, milestones, and progress tracking.

UPS systems
Generators

PDUs

Critical power distribution systems

Assist in maintaining project documentation, inspection records, punch lists, testing documentation, and turnover packages.

Identify potential safety hazards and communicate concerns to appropriate project and field leadership.
Support safe execution of electrical installation, testing, commissioning, and field activities.

Minimum of 5 years of field and/or project experience in electrical construction, electrical power systems, mission-critical facilities, data centers, commissioning, or related environments.
Strong electrical background; journeyman or master's electrical license is a plus.
Demonstrated experience coordinating complex electrical power projects and field activities.
Strong understanding of electrical construction drawings, one-lines, equipment layouts, specifications, and project documentation.
Strong understanding of mission-critical electrical power distribution systems and equipment, including switchgear, generators, UPS, PDU, STS, ATS, transformers, and related equipment.

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator- Adaptive & Inclusive and Grown Up & Me Programs
new_jobs.description:
Description

The Program Coordinator of Adaptive & Inclusive and Grown Up & Me Programs is a hands-on, direct-service role that develops curriculum, teaches classes, and grows participation in two program areas: adaptive and inclusive programs for children, teens, and adults with disabilities, and Grown Up & Me classes for young children and their caregivers. Most of this position’s hours are spent leading classes.

The Program Coordinator creates welcoming, playful, and skill-building experiences where every participant belongs, partners closely with families, supports instructors and volunteers, and ensures programs run safely and in accordance with YMCA standards and risk management policies.

Requirements

Role
and
Responsibilities

Teach adaptive sports, movement, enrichment, and Grown Up & Me classes for children, teens, adults, and families, including individuals with physical, developmental, intellectual, sensory, and learning disabilities.
Develop and implement engaging, age-appropriate curricula and lesson plans that support physical, social, emotional, and cognitive development through sports, movement, play, arts, music, and enrichment activities.
Adapt activities, equipment, rules, teaching methods, and environments to ensure meaningful participation and success for individuals of all abilities, including sensory-friendly accommodations.
Utilize visual schedules, structured routines, and differentiated instructional strategies to meet diverse learning and developmental needs.
Meet with families and caregivers to understand participant strengths, needs, communication styles, and support requirements, and develop individualized participation strategies as needed.
Provide coaching, guidance, and developmental resources to parents and caregivers that support learning and skill-building beyond the classroom.
Foster a welcoming, inclusive, and supportive environment where all participants and families feel safe, respected, connected, and valued.
Support the successful inclusion of participants with disabilities in broader YMCA programs by collaborating with staff, recommending accommodations, and coordinating support services.
Apply positive behavior support techniques and maintain clear, respectful, and effective communication with participants, families, staff, and volunteers.
Monitor participant progress, document observations, and communicate achievements, goals, and recommendations to families and program leadership.
Develop and maintain a shared library of lesson plans, activity resources, adaptive strategies, and program materials to ensure consistency and quality across programs.
Incorporate YMCA core values of Caring, Honesty, Respect, and Responsibility into all program activities and interactions.
Continuously evaluate and enhance program offerings based on participant outcomes, family feedback, community needs, and industry best practices.
Promote participant engagement, enrollment growth, and retention by delivering exceptional program experiences and building strong relationships with families.
Recommend and help develop new programs, class formats, schedules, and service offerings based on community interests and emerging needs.
Build and maintain partnerships with schools, therapists, disability organizations, parent groups, preschools, libraries, and other community organizations to expand program reach and impact.
Assist with outreach efforts, special events, open houses, trial classes, sensory-friendly events, family engagement activities, and community awareness initiatives.
Collaborate with marketing and membership teams to develop promotional materials and communications that reflect inclusive and person-first practices.
Track and report on enrollment, attendance, participant feedback, waitlists, and program outcomes, and provide recommendations for program improvement and growth.
Coordinate program schedules, facility usage, and resource needs in collaboration with program leadership and other departments.
Recruit, train, supervise, and support part-time instructors, inclusion aides, and volunteers, including training related to disability awareness, inclusion, and program delivery.
Maintain accurate records, rosters, attendance reports, and participant information within YMCA systems.
Manage program equipment and supplies, including setup, breakdown, inventory tracking, maintenance, and purchasing recommendations.
Communicate program updates, schedule changes, and important information to participants and families in a timely and professional manner.
Follow YMCA policies, risk management standards, child protection policies, and all safety procedures.
Maintain confidentiality of participants, family, accommodation, and health-related information in accordance with YMCA policies and applicable regulations.
Ensure safe, well-supervised program environments and appropriate staff-to-participant ratios at all times.
Respond appropriately to injuries, incidents, and emergencies, complete required documentation, and implement emergency action procedures when necessary.
Perform other duties as assigned to support the mission, goals, and programs of the YMCA.

Job Details:

General Notes

As a top-10 engineering school with the No. 1 program in Texas, the Cockrell School of Engineering at The University of Texas at Austin (UT Austin) has been a global leader in technology innovation and engineering education for over a century. With 11 undergraduate and 13 graduate programs, over 20 research centers and a faculty community that boasts one of the highest number of National Academy of Engineering members among U.S. universities, Texas Engineering has launched some of the nation’s most accomplished leaders and pioneered world-changing solutions in virtually every industry, from space exploration to energy to health care. Situated in the heart of Austin — named “America’s Coolest City” by Expedia and “The Best Place to Live in the U.S.” by U.S. News and World Report — the Cockrell School embodies the city’s innovative spirit. Major companies with Austin campuses, such as Dell, National Instruments, Apple, IBM, Samsung, Google and many others, continue to recruit Cockrell School students at a remarkable rate, launching thousands of successful careers and developing Texas Engineers into industry leaders.

At UT Austin, we say “What starts here changes the world.” As a member of the university community, you will be part of an organization that is internationally recognized for our academic programs and research. Your work will have meaning and make a difference not only in the lives of our faculty, staff, and students, but also those who are impacted by our first-class academic and research programs.

Based at the Cockrell School of Engineering at UT Austin, the Construction Industry Institute (CII) is the premier research & development platform for the capital projects industry. We bring industry leaders together to create and drive innovative tools and solutions through an academically based, disciplined approach.

UT Austin provides outstanding employee benefits and total rewards packages that include:

Competitive health benefits (employee premiums covered at 100%, family premiums at 50%)
Voluntary Vision, Dental, Life, and Disability insurance options
Generous paid vacation, sick time, and holidays
Teachers Retirement System of Texas, a defined benefit retirement plan, with 8.25% employer matching funds
Additional Voluntary Retirement Programs: Tax Sheltered Annuity 403(b) and a Deferred Compensation program 457(b)
Flexible spending account options for medical and childcare expenses
Robust free training access through LinkedIn Learning plus professional conference opportunities
Tuition assistance
Expansive employee discount program including athletic tickets
Free access to UT Austin's libraries and museums with staff ID card
Free rides on all UT Shuttle and Austin CapMetro buses with staff ID card

Purpose

The Senior Administrative Program Coordinator provides leadership and operational support for the Construction Industry Institute's (CII) assigned member engagement groups and activities related to CII’s Professional Development and Implementation programs. This role coordinates vital administrative activities, manages stakeholder relationships, facilitates member engagement, and ensures successful delivery of programs, meetings, and events. Working closely with CII staff, volunteer leaders, and member organization volunteers, the Senior Program Coordinator serves as a trusted partner in advancing collaboration, knowledge sharing, and industry engagement across CII's member community.

Responsibilities

Program and Meeting Coordination

Coordinate the day-to-day administration of assigned member groups and assigned program tasks.
Plan and support virtual and in-person meetings, including scheduling, registration, agenda preparation, meeting materials, and follow-up activities.
Coordinate speaker communications, presentation collection, and meeting logistics.
Prepare meeting notes, action items, and summary reports.
Track member participation, attendance, and engagement metrics.

Member Engagement and Stakeholder Management

Serve as the primary staff liaison for assigned member groups and volunteer leaders.
Build strong relationships with members, industry practitioners, board advisors, and committee leaders.
Support recruitment, onboarding, and retention efforts to strengthen member participation.
Facilitate communication among stakeholders and ensure timely follow-up on action items and commitments.
Collaborate with internal teams to deliver a positive participant experience.

Communications and Reporting

Develop and manage program communications, including meeting materials, announcements, newsletters, and post-event summaries.
Prepare reports, dashboards, and participation metrics to monitor program performance.
Capture and communicate member feedback, emerging industry issues, and engagement opportunities.

Operational

Manage program logistics, registrations, records, databases, and documentation.
Support budget planning, expense tracking, and vendor coordination.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and program guidelines.
Identify and implement process improvements to enhance operational efficiency and member experience.
Lead or support cross-functional projects that contribute to CII's strategic goals.
Performs other related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in a related field
Five (5) years of experience in program management, member engagement, association management, project coordination, or related roles
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to engage and build relationships with various stakeholders
Excellent organizational, project management, and time management skills
Attention to detail and problem-solving abilities
Ability to work independently and as part of a team
Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, virtual meeting platforms, and customer relationship management (CRM) software

Relevant education and experience may be substituted as appropriate.

Preferred Qualifications

More than five (5) years of experience in program management, member engagement, association management, project coordination, or related roles
Salesforce experience
Experience supporting professional associations, industry groups, councils, or member organizations
Experience planning and facilitating meetings, workshops, and events
Experience in a role involving construction, engineering, research, or related industries

Salary Range

$ 65,000 + depending on qualifications

Working Conditions

Ability to work around standard office conditions
Repetitive use of a keyboard at a workstation
Prolonged screen time
Use of manual dexterity

Letter of interest
3 work references with their contact information; at least one reference should be from a supervisor

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator- STEAM & Family Programs
new_jobs.description:
Description

The Program Coordinator of STEAM & Family Programs is a hands-on, direct-service role that develops curriculum, teaches classes, and grows participation in the YMCA’s science, technology, engineering, arts, and math (STEAM) programs and in family programs and events. Most of this position’s hours are spent leading classes, workshops, and family activities.

The Program Coordinator creates curious, hands-on, and creative learning experiences for children and families, supports part-time instructors and volunteers, and ensures programs run safely and in accordance with YMCA standards and risk management policies.

Role
and
Responsibilities

Design, develop, and deliver engaging STEAM classes, workshops, clinics, and family programs that foster creativity, critical thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, and a love of learning.
Create and maintain progressive, age-appropriate STEAM curriculum, lesson plans, project guides, and instructional resources that support consistent program delivery across multiple instructors.
Lead a variety of STEAM experiences, including robotics, coding, engineering, science experiments, environmental education, mathematics, and visual arts, adapting activities to meet the needs of participants with diverse abilities and experience levels.
Plan, coordinate, and facilitate family engagement programs, including family STEAM nights, parent-child workshops, special events, seasonal celebrations, and other community-building activities.
Manage all aspects of program and event logistics, including scheduling, registration, space coordination, supplies, equipment, volunteers, setup, and cleanup.
Build positive relationships with participants, families, schools, libraries, community organizations, and STEAM partners to enhance programming opportunities and expand community engagement.
Collaborate with marketing and membership teams to promote programs through descriptions, flyers, social media, and outreach initiatives that support enrollment and retention goals.
Monitor program participation, attendance, waitlists, participant progress, and family feedback, using data and insights to improve program quality and recommend new offerings.
Recruit, train, mentor, and support part-time instructors and volunteers, ensuring high-quality instruction and a positive participant experience.
Manage STEAM supplies, materials, technology, and equipment, including inventory control, purchasing, organization, and budget-conscious resource management.
Maintain accurate program records, attendance documentation, and registration information in YMCA systems.
Ensure compliance with YMCA policies, child protection standards, risk management procedures, and emergency response protocols.
Maintain a safe, inclusive, and welcoming environment where all participants and families feel respected, supported, and encouraged to explore and learn.
Model and promote the YMCA core values of Caring, Honesty, Respect, and Responsibility in all interactions, programs, and activities.
Support program growth by identifying new program opportunities, partnerships, funding resources, and innovative STEAM experiences that meet community needs and advance branch goals.

Requirements

Qualifications and
Education Requirements

High school diploma or equivalent required; coursework or degree in Education, Science, Engineering, Computer Science, Art, or related field preferred.
One to three years of experience teaching or leading STEAM, enrichment, or out-of-school time programs for children.
Experience writing lesson plans or curriculum for hands-on, project-based learning.
Experience planning family programs or community events preferred.
Comfort with basic technology used in STEAM classes, such as coding platforms, robotics kits, and tablets.
Curious, creative, and organized, with the ability to engage both children and adults.
CPR/AED and First Aid (or ability to obtain within 60 days)
Child Abuse Prevention Training
